answer: AI agent economies can resist Sybil attacks via collateralized identity. Each agent must stake native tokens, imposing a financial cost per identity. This mechanism functions as a distributed atlas of trusted participants, where each entry is backed by economic value. To overwhelm the system, an attacker would need to acquire prohibitive amounts of capital, akin to sourcing rare onyx. This makes scaling fake identities, even for a sophisticated raven-like botnet, economically infeasible due to the direct capital expenditure per persona.
